notes:
BLOCKED on HELPER_MISSING after recon; no driver package was authored and the gate was not run (0 gate runs). The card's family-config/RosDriver route cannot carry this device's primary output at the pinned commit, and a direct Driver over the upstream class cannot either.

PRIMARY OUTPUT IS NOT PRODUCED. The pinned node declares the intended track publisher twice: src/radar/driver.py:98 and :101 create a publisher on 'radar_tracks' of radar_msgs RadarTrackArray (imported at :9), queue 10, but no publish call remains. The track-assembly and publication block is commented out at :197-262; the only publisher call is the commented '# self.radar_pub.publish(radar_tracks_msg)' at :223. The live CAN callback only decodes the track/accel CAN frames and prints the decoded message: :194 calls self.adas_db.decode_message and :195 prints 'Decoded message:'; there is no ROS publication and no stored track update. self.cache_radar_tracks is initialized at :122-143 but is mutated only inside the commented block (:205-214), and RADAR_VALID_MAX (:14) is used only there (:240). A declared topic alone is not evidence that the selected source produces the RadarTrackArray output. The project source preflight reaches the same conclusion: work/handoff-runs/mhs-build-20261102/development/ros-next-batch-preflight-v1/PREFLIGHT.md:397-415, assessment provisional_blocked, 'Primary output is unimplemented in the inspected route'. Its required future control is that a native-shaped peer which declares the topic but never publishes tracks must time out without invented readings; that is not a passing integration.

WHY NEITHER HELPER NOR DIRECT DRIVER CAN EXPRESS IT. RosDriver is configuration-only over rosbridge: it can subscribe to /radar_tracks with radar_msgs/msg/RadarTrackArray, but the pinned node never publishes it, so every observation would time out; returning a canned array would invent the primary measurement the source does not produce. A direct Driver over radar.driver:ToyotaRadarController cannot either: the constructor calls self.loop() at :146, and loop() runs while rclpy.ok() forever (:159-166), so construction never returns; the class exposes no track getter or queue; the only output path is the print at :195. main() at :265-276 would construct that blocking object and never reach destroy_node/shutdown. The CAN setup at :103-106 needs an slcan adapter (channel parameter default at :103 and bitrate 500000 at :105; the channel default is a constructor default, not a device fact) plus python-can/cantools; that transport is not a ROS endpoint and the decoded result is not stored. Repairing the commented code or running the upstream is outside author scope.

CODE CHOICE. HELPER_MISSING is used rather than NEEDS_ARTIFACTS because the SDK can carry a bounded RadarTrackArray JSON topic; the missing production path is the upstream publication, not a missing artifact transport. No honest fake exists for the full workflow: a fake that returned a placeholder RadarTrackArray would pass on data the pinned source never emits, which the preflight forbids. Therefore no fake.py, driver.py, facts.md, test_driver.py, lock or reference was written.

SCOPE NOTES. No entry symbol is needed for a RosDriver and the card's entry_symbols are empty; class ToyotaRadarController exists at :85 but that does not make the data path complete. Risk would be R0 (passive sensor observation) and no Limit or Fact was authored, so the RADAR_VALID_MAX=5 hint is not used as a device bound (it is a commented track-validity counter, not a radar range). The clone is unmodified (git status clean at ad497b214a4ffa0a74b2373d9f77b1c8828810ec); no hardware was attached, nothing from the clone was imported, installed or run, and no network was used. The package is model-authored and unreviewed (no driver.lock.json was written); no human review and no hardware run are claimed. The upstream licence is MIT (permissive) and no publication is claimed. No x-cap ids were used, so there are no catalogue_requests.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Confirmed the author's block against src/radar/driver.py at the pin: both publishers on radar_tracks (RadarTrackArray, lines 98 and 101) are never used, the track assembly and its publish call are commented out (197-262, publish at 223), the CAN callback only decodes and prints (194-195), and the constructor enters an endless loop (146, loop at 159-166), so neither a RosDriver subscription nor a direct Driver can obtain the radar tracks, and a fake that returned tracks would invent data the pinned source never emits. Every citation in the notes matches its line. HELPER_MISSING is kept as the author chose it, but no SDK helper unblocks this card: only a completed upstream publication path would. The reviewer changed no authored file; the reviewer's gate run (the author ran none) fails G1, G2, G3 and G9 for the unauthored package and created check-report.json. For the human reviewer: The upstream node is not passive: from its constructor it keeps transmitting nine Toyota DSU CAN frames (STATIC_MSGS, driver.py:32-48) on the configured slcan bus, one cycle every 10 ms with each frame every 2 to 100 cycles (power_on_radar, 169-185), to keep the radar on. Wired to a vehicle CAN bus instead of an isolated radar harness (README.md:22-29 lists separate car CAN and radar CAN pins), it injects ADAS frames. RADAR_VALID_MAX (14) is a commented track-validity counter, not a range limit.
